proposals.name: Byl Hasbaine
proposals.entry:
Home: Nine Spoons
Known associate: Lott
Occupation: Street magician, confidence artist, pickpocket, and illegal wizard
Weapon: Rapier

Byl Hasbaine is a lanky albino street magician from Nine Spoons. He wears a towering top hat and a threadbare tuxedo jacket, and carries a rapier like a gentleman—though he is emphatically no gentleman. He can barely read.

Byl began as a stage magician, surviving through sleight of hand, confidence tricks, theft, and the useful human desire to believe an entertaining lie. Somewhere along the way, his tricks stopped being entirely false.

Byl is a Wild Operator: an illegal wild mage who requires no wand, stave, formal education, or spellbook. Wild Operators are extremely rare, profoundly alarming to respectable magicians, and actively sought by the authorities.

His magic works through performance, symbolism, folklore, dreams, coincidence, intuition, and absolute conviction. Frequently, neither Byl nor his audience knows precisely when the trick became real.

In Nine Spoons, Byl is not merely known as a street magician and confidence artist. He has a reputation. Those familiar with him understand that his shabby clothes and comic manner conceal a genuinely dangerous opponent.

Byl worries about the Fogport Constabulary—particularly Inspector Adelaide Voss, who has taken an interest in him. Fortunately, constables seldom venture deeply into Nine Spoons. The neighborhood’s tangled streets, hostile residents, hidden passages, and general contempt for authority afford him considerable protection. That protection ends whenever Byl leaves the Spoons.

Byl is a trickster, not merely a nice man. He lies, bluffs, steals, manipulates, embarrasses bullies, outsmarts authorities, and cheats expectations. His compassion is genuine; his methods are not always respectable. Justice matters more to him than rules.

Humor is Byl’s armor. He laughs in dangerous situations, especially when he is frightened.

He and Lott have been companions for many years. Their friendship began in Nine Spoons and is old, comfortable, and largely unexplained.

Fate Character

High Concept: Street Magician Who Learned the Wrong Magic
Trouble: The Trick That Backfired Knows My Name
Refresh: 3

Other Aspects

  • Nothing Up My Sleeve Except Reality
  • Every Secret Has a Price
  • The Fog Watches Back

Skills

  • Superb (+5): Occult
  • Great (+4): Deceive
  • Good (+3): Burglary, Notice
  • Fair (+2): Stealth, Rapport, Will
  • Average (+1): Athletics, Fight, Shoot, Lore

Stunts

Now You See It…: Once per scene, after successfully creating an advantage with Deceive or Burglary, Byl may disappear from an opponent’s attention. He has not become invisible—they simply stop thinking about him long enough for him to slip away or reposition.

Street Hands: Byl gains +2 to Burglary when palming, planting, stealing, or retrieving a small object through sleight of hand.

Impossible Operation: Once per session, Byl may attempt an Occult operation without preparation or the usual materials. The intended effect may be possible, but the method and consequences are determined by the strange logic of magic.

Magic

Byl performs Operations: improvised magical acts constructed from tricks, stories, props, declarations, symbolism, and certainty. Magic always balances itself. The easier an Operation appears, the stranger its consequences may be. Every impossible act risks leaving a Scar upon reality.

Byl has not yet discovered the dependable signature technique that will eventually be recognized throughout Fogport as uniquely his.

Equipment

Rapier: A gentleman’s weapon carried by a man who is no gentleman. When weapon ratings are used, it is Weapon:1.

Magician’s Effects: Cards, coins, string, chalk, envelopes, concealed pockets, and whatever apparently useless object the present trick requires.

Current Expedition: A pistol with thirty wooden bullets, in addition to his rapier.

Stress and Consequences

  • Physical Stress: 2 boxes
  • Mental Stress: 3 boxes
  • Consequences: Mild (2), Moderate (4), Severe (6)

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — Byl Hasbaine
posts.entry:
Do not reveal directly to the player.

  • As a starving teenager, Byl performed a coin-vanishing trick for a little girl. When she asked him to make it disappear “for real,” he did.
  • What became of the coin remains unresolved.
  • The identity and fate of the little girl remain unresolved.
  • Why Byl possesses the natural ability of a Wild Operator remains unresolved.
  • How the authorities learned about him remains unresolved.
  • Precisely what Inspector Adelaide Voss intends to do when she catches him remains unresolved.
  • The nature of the Whisper, and whether it is separate from Byl, remains unresolved.
  • Byl’s eventual signature magical technique must be discovered through play, not invented retroactively.

Do not resolve these questions by improvisation. They remain live campaign mysteries until Daniel establishes the answers through play or direct canon.

artwork.visual_description: A full-color vertical portrait of Byl Hasbaine in Nine Spoons: a lanky albino Wild Operator in a towering battered top hat and threadbare gentleman's clothes, holding an old coin above an impossible smoke-shadow with one hand near his worn rapier. Blue-green harbor fog and uneven amber gaslight place him firmly in Fogport.
